explained.headline: Russian airstrikes hit Kyiv ahead of trilateral talks

happened.text: Russian forces launched a missile and drone attack on Kyiv and surrounding areas, damaging residential buildings, energy facilities and a bridge.
Ukrainian authorities reported that one person was killed and several others were wounded in the overnight assault.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia deployed 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles during the bombardment.

background.text: Vitali Klitschko is the mayor of Kyiv, the Ukrainian capital affected by recent power and infrastructure disruptions.
Moscow and Kyiv have engaged in intermittent diplomatic discussions mediated by the United States ahead of upcoming meetings in Abu Dhabi.

matters.text: President Zelenskyy asserted that Moscow is attempting to force Ukraine into a complete blackout by targeting vital utility infrastructure.

uncertain.text: Previous rounds of talks have failed to produce breakthroughs, leaving major territorial and security questions unresolved.
Ukrainian officials continue to seek specific, written guarantees from Western allies regarding how postwar security support will function.

why: The evidence confirms Zelenskyy's role and the war's duration, though the claim is not about the specific development.

removed.text: US President Donald Trump stated that the war could be close to a settlement and envisioned a major agreement involving Europe and Moscow.
why: The evidence reflects Trump's stated vision for the agreement.

explained.headline: Paraguay's president impeached and placed under house arrest following bank collapse

happened.text: Santiago Peña, Paraguay's president, has been impeached and placed under house arrest following the collapse of Ueno Bank.
The collapse of the digital bank froze the savings of approximately three million depositors, leaving more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts.
Pedro Alliana, the former vice-president, was sworn in as the new interim president until 2028 and promised that affected citizens would be fully compensated.

background.text: The Paraguayan central bank placed the lender under resolution and seized it after determining that it had breached minimum solvency requirements.

matters.text: Analysts say Santiago Peña is likely to face prosecution over the bank's collapse now that he has been stripped of his immunity.
The crisis severely damages public trust and financial stability.

uncertain.text: It remains unclear when the affected customers will actually receive their money back or what will happen to deposits exceeding the legally protected maximum.
Santiago Peña has denied any wrongdoing, and his defence lawyer Ricardo Preda described the allegations as a reckless and opportunistic accusation.

terms.definition: The Paraguayan social security agency responsible for managing pensions and social welfare payments.
A constitutional process in which a legislature brings charges against a public official for misconduct.

removed.text: Santiago Peña, an economist who took power in August 2023, held shares until last year in the company that owned Ueno Bank.
Ueno Bank belongs to Grupo Vázquez, a large Paraguayan conglomerate, and expanded rapidly after receiving authorisation to operate as a digital bank in 2023.
Thousands of citizens took to the streets in protest, leading to clashes with police who used tear gas and water cannons.
why: Evidence does not confirm the protests were caused by the impeachment.

removed.text: The institution had grown to manage hundreds of millions of dollars in public and pension funds, including deposits from the Instituto de Previsión Social.
why: The claim states reports as facts without proper attribution to media reports.

removed.text: Senator Rafael Filizzola described the situation as the largest corruption scandal in the country's democratic history, calling it a tremendous blow to state credibility.
why: The claim presents the quote as an objective fact rather than a senator's opinion.

removed.text: Investigations are ongoing into whether the bank extended excessive loans to related companies and whether regulatory oversight was manipulated.
why: The claim states investigation focus as fact without citing the ongoing impeachment charges.

explained.headline: Donald Trump appoints Stephen Miller as new White House chief of staff

happened.text: Donald Trump announced via social media that Stephen Miller would replace Susie Wiles as White House chief of staff.
The announcement followed a midterm election defeat in which Democrats won control of the United States Congress.

background.text: Stephen Miller has served as deputy chief of staff and is known as a key architect of Donald Trump's immigration and mass deportation policies.
Susie Wiles had held the position of White House chief of staff since the inauguration in January 2025.
Stephen Miller joined Donald Trump's political campaigns as a speechwriter starting in 2016.

matters.text: Public commentators and political analysts view the appointment as a clear signal that the administration intends to confront rather than cooperate with the newly empowered opposition in Congress.
Public commentators suggest the choice acts as a warning shot to lawmakers.

uncertain.text: Some Republican politicians publicly questioned whether the choice of such a polarizing figure was wise given the recent electoral defeat.
It remains unclear how the White House will manage governance and policy implementation alongside a legislative branch controlled by the opposing party.

terms.definition: The senior aide to the president of the United States who manages White House staff and oversees presidential operations.

removed.text: Democratic leaders stated that their congressional majorities would actively oppose the new agenda.
While Donald Trump's allies celebrated the decision, Democratic lawmakers strongly condemned the appointment.
why: Evidence supports Democratic condemnation, but lacks information on celebration by Trump's allies.
